thread:
sam_support: FYI — customer @jane_customer reporting intermittent 5xxs from the hosted inference API (text-generation) starting ~09:40 UTC. They see gateway/5xx responses. Can we triage?

jane_customer: hitting our app via Redwood, example: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'`

jane_customer: response we get (request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d):
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: rq_0a1b2c3d
{
  "error": "upstream error: controlplane: auth/session: 502",
  "retryable": false
}
```

sam_support: Thanks — can you paste full X-Request-ID and the model/route you were calling (model id + route name)? Also SDK version if possible.

jane_customer: request ids: rq_0a1b2c3d, rq_0a1b2c3e; model: rwd-ggml-small-v1; route: default-chat-64. SDK: js@2.1.0. Errors happen ~20-30% of calls during a ~15m window.

sam_support: escalating to oncall and eng: @eva_oncall @mike_eng — customer impact, lots of 5xx from control-plane deps (auth/session and routing policy).

deploy-bot: Incident created INC-21625 — severity: high — channel #support.

eva_oncall: Looking. I can see a spike in 502/504s for the hosted gateway around 09:40-09:58 UTC. Preliminary traces point to timeouts on routing-policy service when it fetches per-tenant routing rules from config-db. Sample internal log: 
```
2026-02-14T09:41:12.345Z router-1 routing-policy fetch tenant=acct_987 err="context deadline exceeded" upstream=postgres://config-db:5432
2026-02-14T09:41:12.346Z auth-proxy request_id=rq_0a1b2c3d err="session lookup failed: timeout"
2026-02-14T09:41:13.001Z gateway request_id=rq_0a1b2c3d status=502 latency=420ms
```

mike_eng: Repro steps for devs: run the same route through the control-plane proxy locally, watch routing-policy RPCs and configdb connections. Example curl against control-plane (internal):
```
curl -v -H "X-Account: acct_987" http://controlplane.internal.local/v1/route-check
# watch logs from routing-policy service
kubectl logs -l app=routing-policy -n controlplane --since=10m
```

luis_sre: Observed config-db connection pool exhaustion — config-db (single writer pool) hit max_conn ~ 180 and started queueing, which made routing-policy RPCs hit timeouts and bubble up 502s. Root cause: token-refresh storm from our auth session refresher that retries aggressively when control-plane replies are slower, causing thundering refreshes.

luis_sre: Immediate mitigations we applied at 09:50 UTC:
- increased config-db pool from 20 -> 100 for routing-policy read pool (hotfix)
- enabled a short-circuit static routing fallback for tiered accounts to avoid routing-policy calls for known routes
- added 100ms jitter + exponential backoff to the token refresher to reduce retry stampede
- soft restart of 3 routing-policy pods (rolling restart)

mike_eng: Deployed PR #3142 which bumps pool size and adds client-side backoff. Also added a 1s per-host retry delay in the control-plane proxy. Patch diff snippet:
```
- pool_size = 20
+ pool_size = 100
+ retry_policy = { initial_backoff_ms = 100, factor = 2.0, max_backoff_ms = 1000 }
```

eva_oncall: Customer confirmation: @jane_customer can you confirm if errors stopped after ~09:58?

jane_customer: Confirmed — errors dropped to normal levels after ~09:58. Thanks for the quick action. Our side saw a ~4x throughput drop while erroring though, so we had retries.

sam_support: I'll send a follow-up note to the customer summarizing the root cause and the temporary mitigations. Proposed text: 
> We observed timeouts in the control-plane routing-policy service caused by config-db connection saturation. We applied multiple mitigations (pool increase, fallback routing, backoff) which resolved the issue. We'll follow up with a permanent fix and a timeline.

luis_sre: Follow-ups (action items):
- write postmortem and link INC-21625 (owner: luis_sre)
- add SLO/alert: config-db connection saturation threshold + routing-policy 5xx rate alert (owner: mike_eng)
- audit token refresher retry logic across services (owner: eva_oncall)
- consider read-replica for routing-policy reads (infra/DB to evaluate)

mike_eng: Also will add a per-route circuit-breaker so a noisy tenant doesn't take down routing-policy for others.

eva_oncall: Marking incident resolved in the console. Closing thread once postmortem is filed.

sam_support: I'll follow up with the customer's support ticket text and credits offer (if needed). Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
